results.reasoning: Probed through the real CLI (no server, no port used) on a throwaway project with fresh HOME and WALKDOWN_HOME: blueprints new --commit spec, six rules with signoff [eng], a node:test runner recorded via `walkdown run`, one agent run record, and threads via `threads new/set`. `walkdown status` and `--json` show: an open person's note on an agent-passed rule gives the agent 'address n-0002' and, as the narrowed statement intends, still a person's 'walk down' beside it; a person's answered question gives 'incorporate q-0003' and removes the rule's walk-down item, and on an unbuilt rule (q-0004) removes even the wording approval, so a rule holding an answered question is queued to no person; a built rule demanding checks with no claiming check (agent-passed cover2) is 'cover' alone with no person item, while an unbuilt uncovered rule is 'cover' plus wording approval (no judgment of a build); a checks-passed rule never agent-judged is 'judge-first' with no signer; rewording a passed rule makes it 'judge ... stale' with no signer; an agent fail with its finding later set addressed --as-agent is 'judge again' (rejudge, after fail) and nobody else's. Every step holds, and the statement holds in each probe. Edges under 10%: none beyond hand-written arrangements, which are out of scope.
